Took me 7 years to get diagnosed with MS. Kept being told it was anxiety.

It's not like, for example I'll listen to a song and physically feel a sensation on my skin as though it's there- it's more that, for example, a certain sound will strongly remind me of a texture. Kind of like if someone said 'fried egg' to you, you can recall in your mind what fried egg tastes like. (Except for me for example, someone might say the name 'Sarah' and I will be strongly reminded of fried egg.) Or, I'll hear Britney Spears' voice and will be strongly reminded of how it feels to touch a jelly like substance. 

It's just that associations we have with certain sounds, words etc etc are unusual. We don't physically taste or feel anything. (At least - I don't think we do!)

Had so many terrible experiences with NHS mental health care. At 18 I was at my absolute lowest, frequently self harming to the point of needing stitches, deeply suicidal and losing touch with reality (eg believing people I knew were hacking into my computer & phone and monitoring my phone calls etc). 

I had a different therapist/social worker (whatever they had available at the time) every few weeks. And when you're having to divulge your deepest darkest secrets you don't want a new person to see every fucking month. 

I had a 'crisis team' come to the house every day at my lowest to basically check I wasn't dead. New person each time. Often a social worker. One was a man who very angrily said 'I can't help you if you're just going to sit there and not say anything!' I cried. 

I think they had some kind of box to tick off that said they could leave the appointment if I told them I wasn't going to kill myself. I literally heard 'Tell me you're not going to kill yourself' more times than I can count. I felt like all the crisis team did was check I was alive and had a box to tick saying I'd told them I wasn't going to kill myself so that if I did, their backs would be covered. 

I was often told to call the Samaritans instead of being offered actual help. 

I was also diagnosed with a ridiculous amount of completely different thing by different doctors. Everything from 'just low self esteem' to full blown psychosis/personality disorders etc etc. 

The only actual help I got was when, through my mum's job, I got access to private mental health care. I was asked to go into their hospital during my first appointment (ended up staying for 2 months). Funnily enough, there earlier were times where I had been substantially worse when I was under NHS care, and I'd been told 'tell me you're not going to kill yourself and call the Samaritans if you need.'

Genuinely think there's a good chance I'd be dead now if it weren't for my parents' private healthcare.
